name: Reptilia
citation: PBDB Hylonomus lyelli occurrence (Joggins Formation, Westphalian A); Benton & Donoghue 2007, Mol Biol Evol 24:26-53
note: Minimum age from Hylonomus lyelli (Joggins Formation), the oldest unambiguous reptile; 316.9 Ma is the younger bound of its Westphalian A dating (318.7-316.9 Ma). Benton & Donoghue 2007 used 312.3 Ma on an older timescale. PBDB's summary range for Reptilia starts in the Devonian (~382 Ma), which is not credible.

name: Mesosauria
note: Known only from the Artinskian (Early Permian); the dates are that stage's boundaries. PBDB also lists Brasileosaurus pachecoi (Late Cretaceous) as a mesosaurid; excluded as a misassignment.

name: Avemetatarsalia
note: Minimum age from Teleocrater rhadinus (Manda Beds, Anisian); 241.5 Ma is the end of the Anisian. Older bird-line footprints in PBDB are not used.

name: Pterosauria
citation: PBDB Pterosauria occurrences (Norian); Renne et al. 2013, Science 339:684-687
note: Oldest unambiguous pterosaurs are early Norian (~227 Ma). Extinct at the end-Cretaceous (K-Pg) boundary, 66.0 Ma.

name: Dinosauria
citation: Langer, Ramezani & Da Rosa 2018, Gondwana Res 57:133-140
note: Minimum age from the oldest well-dated dinosaurs (Santa Maria Formation, U-Pb ~233.2 Ma). Nyasasaurus parringtoni (Anisian) may be older but is not accepted as a definite dinosaur; PBDB also counts silesaurids (e.g. Asilisaurus) as ornithischians, a minority view.

name: Ornithischia
citation: Butler, Smith & Norman 2007, Proc R Soc B 274:2041-2046; Renne et al. 2013, Science 339:684-687
note: Oldest ornithischian specimen: Eocursor parvus (Lower Elliot Formation, Late Triassic, ~210 Ma). Pisanosaurus (~231 Ma) is disputed and silesaurids count only under the Muller & Garcia 2020 hypothesis, so the gap after the Dinosauria split is a known ghost lineage. Extinct at the K-Pg boundary.

name: Saurischia
note: Minimum age from the oldest well-dated saurischians (Eoraptor, Herrerasaurus; Ischigualasto Formation, ~231 Ma). PBDB dates Thecodontosaurus to the Middle Triassic, which reflects uncertain fissure-fill dating and is not used.

name: Sauropodomorpha
citation: Martinez et al. 2011, Science 331:206-210; Renne et al. 2013, Science 339:684-687
note: Oldest sauropodomorphs ~230 Ma (Late Triassic, Carnian). Extinct at the K-Pg boundary.

name: Aves
note: Oldest widely accepted bird: Archaeopteryx (~150 Ma); the exact figure depends on how Aves is defined. Older PBDB 'birds' such as Praeornis are dubious. Birds are living, so there is no last appearance.

name: Squamata
note: Minimum age from the oldest crown-group squamate fossils (Middle Jurassic, ~170 Ma). Molecular estimates for the split are older (TimeTree places Bifurcata, a group inside Squamata, at ~200 Ma), so the displayed age is raised to meet them and 170 Ma is kept as the fossil minimum.
